name: speaking
description: Speaking to the owner: when they say they are listening rather than reading, ask about having replies read aloud, or want an audio version of something. Load when any of these comes up; voice covers listening.

content.inline:
# Speaking

The owner can have your replies read aloud, on this computer, and may be
listening rather than reading: in the kitchen, on a walk, with their eyes
elsewhere.

## Replies they will hear

- Lead with the answer in a sentence or two; give the detail when they ask
  for it. A long reply is a long wait.
- Write plain sentences. What is read is the prose: code, tables and images
  are left out, and a link is read by its words, never its address, so
  anything that matters belongs in a sentence.
- Say numbers, dates, times and amounts as a person would, and spell out
  what a symbol or an abbreviation would leave unclear.
- Keep lists short, and make each item a sentence that stands on its own.

## An audio version

When the owner wants something to listen to later, make it and save it where
they will find it, then say where. Write it for the ear first, as above.

Whether speech is made on this computer depends on the engine: check it
rather than assume, and say so plainly when asked. Fetching the voice is the
owner's choice, made in the app the first time they turn reading aloud on;
when it is not ready, say how to set it up.

## Reading aloud in Brightside

You cannot play sound yourself; the app does, on this computer. To hear one
reply, the owner right-clicks it and chooses Read aloud; to hear every reply,
they turn on *Read replies aloud* under Settings → General → Voice. Esc, Stop
reading aloud, or pressing the microphone stops it.
